correctness.rationale: Every matrix block and normalization has been rederived. Subtracting the 0th row gives the multiplicative Hankel matrix; its character-inversion decomposition yields the determinant product with correct sign. For a≠0,b≠0, the quadratic vertex u0=-a/(2b) is nonzero and its phase v=-a²/(4b) is nonzero and uniquely achieved. Coprime cyclotomic conductors force all phase coefficients equal if a nontrivial character sum vanishes, contradicting the singleton fiber and zero character sum. The trivial factor has strictly negative real part. For b=0,a≠0 the same criterion applies; for a=0 the rank is exactly the size of the distinct-square Fourier minor by Chebotarev. Numerical SVD checks cover 222 cases across primes 3,5,7,11,13,17,19 without being used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Parabolic Fourier extension is a fundamental finite-field restriction model. Sampling that extension along a second parametrized parabola is a naturally square reconstruction problem. The theorem gives the complete all-prime phase diagram: varying the quadratic frequency coefficient never breaks injectivity when the linear coordinate is present, whereas losing that coordinate produces a forced, explicitly quantified (p-1)/2-dimensional information loss. The singleton-fiber mechanism explains this rigidity beyond a single computed example. It is an exact natural sampling invariant, not an arbitrary finite census.
